newsitem.title: KENYA: Exporters' dollar sales push up Kenya shilling.
newsitem.headline: Exporters' dollar sales push up Kenya shilling.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling strengthened against the dollar and the pound on Friday amid heavy dollar selling by exporters, commercial bank dealers said.
Against the dollar, the Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling rate of 57.10 compared to 58.57 on Thursday, while against the pound the shilling was posted at a mean rate of 95.97 from 98.21.
Dealers said investors rushed into the market to cash in on appreciating rates once it was clear sentiment favoured a stronger shilling.
But they added the shilling's stability was precarious as many foreign investors were trading cautiously.
Donors' threats this week to withhold further aid if the government did not carry out economic and political reforms sent bad signals to foreign investors, dealers said.

"They're nervous and because they're comfortable with the 57 level they could get out. Most of them came in at this level. If they do (get out) they will put more pressure on the shilling," a senior dealer told Reuters.
The money market remained liquid. Overnight rates were quoted at between five and 10 percent compared with five and 12 percent on Thursday.
